headline: Committee hears Molokaʻi residents on budget requests, storm flooding and invasive pest

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: At an in-person Molokaʻi meeting, a speaker asked the committee to put $600,000 back in the budget and residents described storm flooding. The invasive species coordinator said a pest was detected last week and the council will hear shortly if more help is needed.
meeting.recap: The committee chair opened an in-person meeting on Molokaʻi to hear from residents.[[0:00:19]] He asked the committee to put $600,000 for the program back in the budget.[[0:18:16]] A council member said the association missed the deadline when submitting for the budget.[[0:33:38]] The program's coordinator asked the committee to put the program in the budget.[[0:59:06]] A council member said the program would be one of their priority items for Decisions Week.[[0:59:36]] He said the center is asking for $545,000.[[1:04:43]] Family Life Center Molokaʻi asked for continued county funding for its homeless services.[[1:10:44]] A council member said that request is already in the mayor's proposed budget.[[1:28:23]] The island's invasive species coordinator said a pest they feared most was detected on Molokaʻi last week.[[1:34:09]] A council member said people hurt by the recent storms and flooding can apply through the mauirecovers.org webpage.[[1:45:00]]
meeting.next: The invasive species coordinator said the council will hear very shortly if more help is needed. The chair asked anyone with written testimony to submit it to the committee.

moments.q: "They missed the deadline when submitting the budget."

boards.name: Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

issues.oneLine: Residents thanked the council for funding programs that feed keiki and support local farmers.
issues.why: A board member said Kaukau for Keiki feeds children over the summer when school is out.
issues.brief: A farmer thanked the council for supporting the Hawaiʻi Farmers Union farm apprentice mentorship program.[[#1]] A resident said she picked up a bag of fruits and vegetables from Sustainable Molokaʻi.[[#2]]
